newsitem.title: JAPAN: N.KOREA DENIES BASKETBALL STAR DEFECTED TO CANADA.
newsitem.headline: N.KOREA DENIES BASKETBALL STAR DEFECTED TO CANADA.

text.p: North Korea on Wednesday angrily lashed out at rival South Korea for spreading a "rumour" that the world's tallest basketball player, who is from the communist state, had defected to Canada.

"The rumour, spread by the 'Agency for National Security Planning', is a groundless lie and a despicable political drama," said a spokesman for North Korea's Committee for the Peaceful Reunification of the Fatherland.
South Korean media reported this week that Ri Myong-hun, a 2.32-metre (7.61-feet) tall basketball player, had defected to Canada and sought asylum so that he could play with a U.S. professional team.
The 27-year-old Ri, the tallest basketball player in the world, flew to Canada on Wednesday last week.
"Ri went to Canada for professional training in the hope of improving his technique and earning himself a worldwide fame in basketball circles," the North Korean spokesman said in a statement.
The statement was carried by the official Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) monitored in Tokyo.
"He is now engrossed in training, belonging to a team of Canada with which he has made a contract, resolved to exalt the honor of his motherland," the spokesman said.
"His entry into the country and his stay there are very natural in view of sportsmen's international activities. They have nothing to do with 'refuge'," he added.
Canada has told Seoul it has not been contacted by the North Korean basket player, a spokesman for the South Korean Foreign Ministry said on Wednesday.
South Korea raised fears last week over a possible mass influx of "boat people" from hunger-stricken North Korea after two families totalling 14 people made a direct escape by sea to the South.
The largest breakout was by a group of 17 -- including 16 members of a single family -- which arrived in South Korea last December after a six-week long epic escape through China.
Last month North Korea's former top ideologue, Hwang Jang-yop, reached Seoul after defecting in Beijing.
